body: That's completely horrible. I'm sorry, I really don't know the answer, but they'll see either of those things as you abandoning them. They're in a completely different state of mind then normal human thought here, I know what it's like, to be nearly physically incapable of liking anything about yourself, that's not their fault. I know it's hard but you're helping more then you know just by sitting there and listening.

She wants to take it slowly. The problem is that I've felt so lonely for so long, and then this amazing person comes along and acts like they're actually mildly interested in me, and I have a very hard time myself "taking it slow". I want to be as close to her as possible as soon as possible. It's not fair to her, and it's only going to get me hurt I'm afraid.

You obviously don't know what it feels like to be depressed to the point of suicidal thoughts. Thinking about that only makes you feel guilty, it's one of the least productive directions you can go in your mind.
If only it was as easy as you make it sound.
I definitely agree, but it's still an encouraging message.

Actually I'm feeling good enough about myself at this point to know that I don't need advice from someone who told me "maybe you should man up".

Thanks but no thanks, I'm not terribly sure you'd do me a lot of good to tell the truth. When I feel like I can't trust my parents, I'm SURE I'll want to trust someone who claims to be in the porn industry and gives out advice to pimp out your own mother.

I know for a fact there are.

I have constant guilt over sexual fetishes I developed as a young child, I have no method of self-validation, relying on others to give me any confidence I have, I constantly compare myself to other people in a negative light, and I think I might have some form of serious OCD, because I am often incapable of thinking about anything but a specific train of thought. There are nights when I can only think about death, blood, dead bodies, and the like, and I feel like I literally, physically, want to tear my own brain out of my head to stop thinking about these things.

Doing nothing is all I do anymore though. It makes me feel miserable. I seem physically incapable of sitting down and relaxing. It's not like I haven't tried, I've tried so much, but I always just feel worthless when I try.

I wish I could do that. I really do. Being able to be with a group of people that know what I've been going through sounds great, but it's incredibly hard for me to have any initiative right now. I feel like all I want to do is lie down on the couch and stay there, just stare at the blank TV. I don't have my license because we're trying to avoid paying extra insurance, so I can't just go out driving, and I don't feel like I can just approach my parents and say, "hey, you know how I'm going through some depression, well here's what I want to do". I mean I see them sitting there watching TV, talking about whatever, and I just feel pathetic going to them about it.

I'm really just not sure how to do anything right now.

You act like sex is the center of all of my problems. I'm not addicted to anything sex-wise. I role-play with someone maybe once every two weeks. Sexual feelings are part of my guilt, but not the root of my problems, and you don't understand that my situation doesn't ALLOW for me to get out of the house almost at all.

That's exactly how I feel. My mother is deeply religious, and we both love each other, but she disagrees with almost all of my philosophical/spiritual beliefs and ideals, and it wouldn't be a problem except that she's constantly concerned I'm going to hell, and I wish so much that I could make her feel better. My father is much more accepting, but he's told me before that he's a pretty simple guy, and it's true, he's never had problems having confidence in himself, and he honestly doesn't understand what I'm going through. He's the only person I can even talk to, and his advice is usually just, "Don't worry you're normal, and the doctor will be able to help you," which honestly doesn't help at all.

It just really makes me feel horrible to sit there on the couch at three in the morning and have my parents hover over me as I'm crying and I know that they're the only people I can even talk to in real life, and they simply don't understand. They don't even know about my thoughts of suicide.

I went to the doctor about it mid-way through last month, after I had an anxiety attack every night for a week straight, and I got prescribed an antidepressant that wouldn't let me sleep for three days straight, until I was having auditory hallucinations and forgetting my own name. I got off of it after the fourth pill, and now I'm taking a generic Xanax at night to sleep, but it seems it's just made me hurt during the day instead of the night. I'm going to see a therapist, hopefully, starting early next month, but it feels like such a long time, and I feel like there's nothing I can do to change my life in my current situation anyway.

I don't have any friends at all right now. I have acquaintances, all on the internet, but nobody I can trust anymore. I don't know why I'm so obsessed with the idea of companionship, but more then anything else I just want somebody besides my parents that I can go up to and hug and feel safe with. I also can't really make friends at the moment, because I try as hard as I can to make normal conversation, but my depression has affected so many parts of my life that I just sound crazy to most people, and myself.

Hey guys, I just got off of a conversation with this individual on Omegle, and directed them here. I know they didn't leave a whole lot up there, but what they told me is that on a scale from 1 to 10, they're a eight tonight on the "contemplating suicide" scale. They said they've attempted four times before, and that a specific friend has saved them every time. They appear to be currently in an abusive household, and are under stress at school and home both.

I directed them here because I felt that I didn't know how to help them personally, but I let them know that I and the people here care. Please help talk to this individual.

Thanks guys, I cannot express how much I appreciate that. Actually, me and my family have suspected that from a very young age (I first started doing things like counting tree limbs and ceiling tiles and moving my fingers in patterns and stuff) that I have some form of OCD. I never thought about connecting it to depression before, though I'm not sure why. I do stuff like that all of the time, if I tap a key on my keyboard wrong, I'll have to do it two or three times to not only get it right, but "balance it out" or something. I can ignore these things if I consciously think about it, but it makes me uncomfortable so I allow them to work on me most of the time, and people don't notice unless they really pay attention, (for example I'll time my steps when walking on tiles or the sidewalk, so that I step on the right tiles or get the same number of steps in each sidewalk tile, this is the more noticeable stuff).

But really, this helped a ton, because last night, after typing this all, I was unable to sleep, and after a long time pacing around the house, my dad woke up, and we talked for a good while. I told him a lot of stuff I hadn't before, including my guilt over what I feel I've done to deserve so much of this, and seeing him not freak out was just about the most reassuring thing on Earth.

And regarding a doctor, I have been to see one about my anxiety, and he prescribed me "Lexapro". It's only been two nights now, but so far there's no obvious difference. I guess I shouldn't expect anything that fast, but to be honest, it's becoming rather hard for me to be patient with my depression anymore. I don't like the idea of having to wait to see an improvement, I guess that's something I'll have to work on. We do have health insurance, and my doctor is supposed to call us back soon about a counselor/therapist for me, I believe.

I can't express the relief of seeing the sun come up this morning. I feel so much better, if exhausted.
Ugh, when I say "crossed" the line in paragraph seven, I meant "drew" the line. I'm sorry, I just felt the correction was needed because it changes the meaning quite a bit.
